questions.question_text:
Sphere Q has three times the radius of sphere P.
How many times as large is sphere Q's surface area compared with sphere P's?

options.why: Multiplied by the radius factor without squaring it, forgetting the $r^{2}$ in the formula.
Doubled the radius factor instead of squaring it.

questions.solution_text:
Let sphere P have radius $r$, so sphere Q has radius $3r$.
Sphere P: $4\pi r^{2}$
Sphere Q: $4\pi(3r)^{2} = 4\pi(9r^{2}) = 36\pi r^{2}$
$36\pi r^{2} \div 4\pi r^{2} = 9$
Sphere Q's surface area is $9$ times as large, because the radius is squared.
